title: Secret Night Discussion
next_chapter_hook: Just as Mo Xiansheng's figure completely dissolved, a gaze that seemed to come from the abyss of the Nine Hells descended upon Chen Ji without any warning. That feeling of being watched made his back instantly soaked with cold sweat.

text.content:
Midnight, Tianqing Sect Servants' Quarters.

Chen Ji sat alone by the window, the moonlight like frost, making his seemingly ordinary face appear even more unremarkable. The jade slip recording the forbidden coordinates in his hand had been turned over and examined no less than a hundred times, every pattern etched into his mind.

The predecessor's relic.

He murmured to himself, but his eyes were a fathomless abyss of darkness. That place, he shouldn't go. But those transferred resources, those deliberately left traces, clearly beckoned him forward.

A trap, or some unspeakable summoning?

dialogue.content:
"You are hesitating."

An aged and ethereal voice rang out without warning, and Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply. He didn't turn around, only his fingers tightened slightly, causing the jade slip to emit a soft crunching sound.

"Mo Xiansheng." His voice was terrifyingly calm. "What brings you to visit in the deep night?"

text.content:
Mo Xiansheng drifted to Chen Ji's side, standing shoulder to shoulder as they gazed at the night sky beyond the window. The cold moon seemed to sense something too, quietly hiding behind the clouds, plunging the surroundings into darkness.

"You know that place." Mo Xiansheng's voice came as if from ancient times, carrying an unquestionable certainty. "And you know that once you step in, there will be no turning back."

Chen Ji slowly turned around, finally meeting those eyes that seemed capable of seeing through everything. His expression remained that same harmless, timid appearance, but if anyone looked into his eyes at this moment, they would discover that beneath that calm surface, terrifying waves were churning furiously.

"This junior is foolish." He lowered his eyes, his voice as light as a mosquito's buzz. "I humbly request the gentleman's guidance."

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng suddenly laughed, that laugh hoarse and desolate, sounding especially chilling in the silent night.

"Foolish?" He shook his head. "When Chen Xuan chose you back then, he said the same thing. But he never truly saw through you."

The old man raised an ethereal palm, pointing remotely at Chen Ji's heart position. That place seemed empty, but if a grand master were here, they would sense a hint of Heavenly Secrets power dormant within, hidden to the extreme.

"The Tianji Record chose you, not by coincidence." Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly dropped low. "And the blood flowing within you... originates from the same source as the previous master of the Tianji Record."

text.content:
Chen Ji's breath stopped for a moment.

In that instant, a crack finally appeared on his perpetually calm face. The same source? What did that mean? Did it mean the Tianji Record didn't fall into his hands by accident, but rather... his bloodline was summoning it?

"Does the gentleman mean..." He suppressed the raging waves in his heart, yet his voice still maintained its usual steadiness. "This junior has some connection with that previous master?"

Mo Xiansheng gave no direct answer. He simply watched Chen Ji quietly, his gaze revealing a trace of... pity?

dialogue.content:
"Do you know the true meaning of the Heavenly Fate Lock Key?"

Mo Xiansheng's voice suddenly became distant, as if coming from an extremely remote place.

"The reason the Tianji Record requires the consumption of Heavenly Fate Value to operate is because its essence is using life to peer into heaven—exchanging the user's lifespan and luck for that brief three hours of foresight."

He paused, a meaningful light flickering in those ethereal eyes.

"But did you know? There exists a type of person who is inherently compatible with the way of Heavenly Secrets. Their bloodline flows with the instinct to peer into heavenly secrets, and their very existence is a key that can open the door of destiny."

text.content:
Chen Ji's pupils contracted sharply.

Heavenly Fate Lock Key. He had seen this term in some forbidden texts before, considering it merely a legendary existence at that time. But now that Mo Xiansheng spoke of it personally...

"Does the gentleman mean," his voice tightened slightly, "that this junior is the so-called... Heavenly Fate Lock Key?"

Mo Xiansheng shook his head, then nodded.

"You are, yet you are not entirely." The old man's voice grew even lower. "The Lock Key power within you is残缺的, incomplete. If you wish for it to fully awaken..."

His gaze suddenly turned sharp, piercing directly into the deepest part of Chen Ji's heart.

"You need to find her—the person who was taken away."

dialogue.content:
Chen Ji's body shuddered violently.

That name—Chen Nian—like thunder exploding in his mind. His sister, his sister who had been missing for years, the girl taken by the Holy Sect as a "Heavenly Fate Lock Key."

Mo Xiansheng actually knew!

"You've been searching for her all along." Mo Xiansheng's voice held no fluctuation, yet every word cut like a knife. "You thought she was merely a chess piece being used by the Holy Sect, but you don't know that the blood resonance between you and her is the key to unlocking the true secrets of the Tianji Record."

The old man's ethereal form began to fade even more, as if it might dissipate at any moment.

"You thought it was the Tianji Record that chose you on this journey?" His laughter was low and bitter. "No, it was your bloodlines calling to each other. And this... is precisely what that mastermind behind the scenes wants most to see."

text.content:
Chen Ji remained silent for a long time.

The night wind blew through the broken window lattice, swaying the hair at his temples gently. His expression shifted from shock, to deep thought, to a terrifying calm. This process was extremely brief, but for someone who had risen from trash to his current position through careful scheming, it was enough time for him to complete countless calculations in his mind.

"The mastermind behind the scenes." He finally spoke, his voice terrifyingly calm. "Is the gentleman referring to... the Five Elders?"

Mo Xiansheng shook his head, that action seemingly light, yet carrying an undeniable negation.

"The Five Elders are merely chess pieces." His voice suddenly turned ice-cold. "They don't even know they are chess pieces. You think the Holy Sect's invasion, Xuanwu Sect's ambitions, the friction between the three major sects—these are coincidences?"

The old man raised his head, as if gazing at some invisible existence.

"This chess game began the moment you were born."

choice.prompt: The information revealed by Mo Xiansheng was like a sharp blade, piercing directly into the recognition Chen Ji had painstakingly constructed over the years. That the mastermind behind the scenes was actually not the Five Elders? Then who was controlling all of this?

text.content:
Chen Ji raised his head, directly facing Mo Xiansheng's eyes, deep enough to seemingly devour everything. He did not retreat; instead, he took a step forward.

"Since the Five Elders are merely chess pieces, then who is the one playing the game?" His voice remained as calm as ever, yet the edge contained within was impossible to ignore. "Since the gentleman has come visiting in the deep night, surely you wouldn't mind speaking more clearly."

Mo Xiansheng's ethereal form rippled slightly, as if examining this seemingly humble young man. After a moment, he let out a low laugh.

"You are quite composed." A trace of inexplicable appreciation appeared in the old man's voice. "Very well, some things you must know sooner or later."

choices.text: Temporarily accept the implications, hide one's feelings and not act
choices.description: The truth is too heavy; now is not the time for inquiry, lest it alert the enemy. Better to first digest this information and wait for a better opportunity.

text.content:
Chen Ji lowered his eyes, concealing the raging waves in his gaze beneath that calm exterior.

"This junior understands." He respectfully made a bow, his voice still as humble as when he first entered the sect. "Thank you for your guidance, sir."

Mo Xiansheng gazed at him for a moment, then let out a meaningful sigh.

"You, child..." The old man's voice dropped low. "Are more like Chen Xuan than Chen Xuan himself."

There was deeper meaning in these words, but Chen Ji remained composed, simply storing all that information in his heart. The time had not yet come; he would not bare his fangs so easily.

dialogue.content:
Mo Xiansheng's form grew increasingly ethereal, as if it would dissolve into the void at any moment. He glanced at the night sky beyond the window, his brow slightly furrowing.

"Time is running out." He said in a low voice. "There are some things you are learning too early, which will only bring catastrophic disaster. But there are other things you must know in advance..."

The old man's gaze suddenly became extremely sharp, as if wanting to see through Chen Ji's soul.

"The Eye of Heavenly Dao."

The moment these four words were spoken, Chen Ji felt all the hairs on his body stand on end, a inexplicable chill shooting from his tailbone straight to the crown of his head.

"It is not a person, but an existence that transcends the will of Heavenly Dao." Mo Xiansheng's voice grew increasingly distant. "Throughout history, all prophets have merely been chess pieces laid out by it. The Tianji Record... is also merely an eye it uses to observe the world."

text.content:
Chen's breathing came to a complete halt.

The Tianji Record... was merely the eye of the Heavenly Dao? Then everything he had plotted using the Tianji Record over these years—had it all been under the gaze of that "eye"?

He suddenly recalled those bizarre prophecies—those predictions that should have been accurate, yet always deviated at critical moments. He had originally thought it was due to the consumption of Heavenly Fate, but now that he thought about it...

"Those deviations," his voice was hoarse, barely resembling his own, "was the Heavenly Dao's eye interfering?"

Mo Xiansheng gave no answer. Only in those deep eyes was there a layer of sorrow so dense it could not be dissolved.

dialogue.content:
"When Chen Xuan discovered the truth, he was already at the end of his strength." Mo Xiansheng's voice was low and mournful. "He spent his entire life searching for a way to escape the control of the Heavenly Dao's eye, and in the end, only left behind a wisp of soul, guarding the Tianji Record, waiting for the next destined one."

The old man suddenly stretched out his hand, his illusory fingertips gently pressing against Chen's brow center.

A wave of cold air instantly flooded into his mind. Chen felt his vision blur as countless images flashed by like a carousel—

It was a chaotic void, a massive eye gazing down upon all living beings, and within that eye were reflected countless struggling figures...

And right at the center of that eye, a blurred figure was staring back at it. That figure bore a seventy percent resemblance to Chen.

"That is..." Chen's entire body trembled.

"Your ancestor." Mo Xiansheng's voice came from the distance, "the first Heavenly Fate Lock Key."

choice.prompt: The images of the ancestor exploded in his mind like thunder. That figure confronting the Heavenly Dao's eye was actually the source of his bloodline? Chen felt the crushing weight of destiny pressing down upon him like mountains.

text.content:
"The ancestor, he..." Chen's voice was艰涩, "what was his final outcome? Did he fall, or..."

Mo Xiansheng's illusory form fluctuated violently, as if bearing some tremendous pressure.

"He neither perished nor achieved victory." The old man's voice became ethereal. "He only... transformed himself into part of the Heavenly Dao's eye, using this as the price to leave future generations a chance to break free."

Chen's entire body shook, light blazing in his eyes.

"That chance is..."

"It is the blood pulse resonance between you and your sister." Mo Xiansheng continued, "The Heavenly Fate Lock Key is not merely a key—it is simultaneously... a chain."

text.content:
Chen took a deep breath, forcibly suppressing the turbulent waves in his heart. He knew some truths were too heavy and required slow digestion.

"Master," he raised his head, his gaze regaining its calmness and depth, "the Five Elders, the Holy Sect, the Xuanwu Sect... what roles do they play in this chess game?"

Mo Xiansheng glanced at him, a flash of approval in his eyes.

"The Five Elders are puppets controlled by the Heavenly Dao's eye—they themselves are unaware. The Holy Sect... are arrogant ones attempting to exploit the power of the Heavenly Dao's eye. As for the Xuanwu Sect..."

The old man's voice suddenly turned cold.

"They are the only ones in this chess game who have sensed something amiss. That old creature Ling Yuan is far more dangerous than you imagine."

Ling Yuan.

This name was like a basin of ice water poured over his head, extinguishing all the燥热 in Chen's heart. That old sect master who had always shown him "great care"... that seemingly venerable guardian of the Tianqing Sect...

"Is he also a piece of the Heavenly Dao's eye?" Chen's voice tightened.

Mo Xiansheng's form had faded until nearly invisible, just a blurred outline floating in mid-air.

"He is a piece, yet also... another person attempting to manipulate the board." The old man's voice came from all directions, as if from an extremely distant place. "He competed with Chen Xuan for the inheritance of the Tianji Record. After being rejected by the Tianji Record, his heart changed. He believed that obtaining the Tianji Record would allow him to escape the control of the Heavenly Dao's eye."

Mo Xiansheng let out a mournful laugh.

"The tragic thing is—the more he struggles, the deeper he sinks."

dialogue.content:
Chen fell silent.

He thought of Ling Yuan's "care" over the years—seemingly protective on the surface, yet restrictive at every turn. Those seemingly coincidental arrangements, those perfectly-timed "concerns"... now that he thought about it, all were meticulously designed pieces on the board.

Old fox.

He coldly spat out these three words in his heart.

"Master." He suddenly spoke, his voice calm yet firm, "If I wish to break this chess game, where should I begin?"

Mo Xiansheng's form had faded until only a pair of eyes could barely be distinguished, yet within those eyes burst forth unprecedented light.

"Find her." The old man's voice was like from the nine heavens, "Find Chen Nian. Once your blood pulses resonate, it will shake the very foundation of the Tianji Record. At that time, the Heavenly Dao's eye's suppression of you... will greatly weaken."

text.content:
Chen Nian.

That name exploded in his mind like thunder once more. Chen's fists unconsciously clenched tight, his knuckles whitening. His sister, that little girl who had always followed behind him, calling "Brother, brother"...

He remembered that night many years ago. People from the Holy Sect suddenly burst into their home, reducing everything to ashes. And he, having been taken ahead of time by Chen Xuan, narrowly escaped.

All these years, he had been searching for her. Never giving up.

"Where is she?" His voice was dangerously low, "Master, tell me, where is she?"

Mo Xiansheng's form had completely dissipated, leaving only a wisp of residual aura lingering in the air. And that final voice, like a candle in the wind, flickered uncertainly.

"Forbidden Grounds... the ruins of the former master of the Tianji Record... there is..."

The voice cut off abruptly.

Chen raised his head sharply, light blazing in his eyes.

Forbidden Grounds. The ruins of the former master of the Tianji Record. There is... what is there? What were the words Mo Xiansheng did not finish?

He lowered his gaze to his own hands, where he held a Jade Slip recording forbidden coordinates. Coincidence? No, there are no coincidences in this world. Everything is arranged by fate.

That forbidden land he was "absolutely not supposed to set foot in"—the answer was actually there.

Chen slowly stood up and walked to the window. The乌云 in the night sky had dispersed, and that cold moon revealed itself once more, scattering its cold light across his face. His expression was terrifyingly calm, yet deep within those eyes, flames were burning.

"Chen Nian..." he murmured to himself, his voice light as a dream, "Wait for me."

At that moment, all the hair on Chen's body suddenly stood on end.

An unprecedented sense of oppression descended without warning, as if an invisible eye was watching him from the depths of the void. That feeling of being observed was so intense, so real, that it soaked his back in cold sweat instantly.

Heavenly Dao's eye.

It... was watching.

Chen forcibly suppressed the churning in his heart, slowly turned around, and gazed into the void behind him. His expression remained calm as still water, as if noticing nothing.

"Master visiting so late at night truly honors my humble dwelling." His voice carried a slight, hard-to-detect tremor, "I wonder if what Master said earlier was true or false?"

No one answered.

Yet that feeling of being watched pressed down on his heart like a physical thing, impossible to shake.

After a long while, Chen slowly withdrew his gaze.

He sat back down by the window, fingers gently stroking the Jade Slip. Under the moonlight, no emotional fluctuations could be seen on his face, yet only he knew how many turbulent waves churned within his heart at this moment.

Mo Xiansheng's words had completely overturned his years of understanding. The Tianji Record was not an opportunity but a shackle. The Heavenly Dao's eye was not a legend but a sword hanging over his head. The Five Elders were merely pieces, and Ling Yuan was even more scheming...

And his sister Chen Nian was actually the key to breaking all of this.

Chen raised his head and gazed at the night sky outside the window. That cold moon still hung high, but now it looked like a massive eye, gazing down upon all living beings.

"Heavenly Dao's eye..." he murmured to himself, his voice carrying a hint of mockery, "You're watching, aren't you?"

No one replied.

But Chen knew—it was there. It had always been there.
